Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * iPhone revenues remain strong despite staggered launch, partly on channel sell-in and from higher ASPs
  * Gross margins and Services revenue growth are lower in F1Q , and we model them remaining lower over the next few Qs
  * Reiterate Buy. PO of $370 based on approx. 35x C28E EPS

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Revenues strong despite staggered launch

Despite supply constraints impacting iPhone, iPad and Macs, Apple delivered a
strong F4Q26 with iPhone revs growing 17%y/y (double digit growth in the U.S.
and Greater China). Apple guided F1Q27 revs to $154-158bn (+7-10% y/y), higher
than the Street at $153bn as iPhone rev growth remains strong driven by units
(despite staggered launch) and higher ASPs. Monetization opportunity with AI
Siri can drive customers to move up on their iCloud plans. Bears will likely
point to 1) iPhone unit benefit from selling into the channel, 2) iPad and Mac
revs likely continue to benefit from new products in Dec qtr, 3) lower
Services growth driven by regulation, weaker third party services and 4) lower
GM over the next several qtrs. Both inventory and purchase commitments were
much higher, driven by higher memory costs. Reiterate Buy on strong capital
returns, eventual winner on AI at the edge and optionality from new products.

Gross margins sequentially lower on higher memory costs

F4Q overall GM of 47.9%, and product GM of 37.2%, both benefited 100bps from
tariff refunds, and both faced 100bps q/q headwind from higher memory costs.
GM for F1Q was guided to 45-46% (45.5% mid-pt with some tariff benefit). The
decline in GMs is partially offset by 1) cost savings in non-memory
components, 2) benefit of carrying inventory at lower cost (should last a few
more qtrs.) and 3) higher pricing on products.

Is Services growth now structurally lower?

Services rev for F1Q was guided to 8-9% y/y, vs. 10% y/y in F4Q, as 3rd party
licensing rev remains weak, as does App Store rev (lower mix of Mobile
gaming), and on slightly higher FX (0.5% higher impact vs. Sep qtr). In
addition, Apple has made some changes to App Store business model in certain
countries, and in the U.S. continues to operate under a court ruling impacting
link-out transactions. Services GM in F1Q see higher cloud costs for Siri AI
which would be recognized as Services cost of sales. In the l-t, we see
Services revs reaccelerating as the IB remains underpenetrated, and we see
room to expand Services revs as Apple starts to monetize AI Siri related
applications.

Adjusting estimates; PO $370

We model F27E rev/EPS of $537bn/$9.15 (prior $526bn/$9.12). Our PO of $370 is
based on approximately 35x our C28E EPS of $10.32.

| | | MRVL/LITE underscores the strategic value of scarce optical assets, reinforced by LITE's strong results and NPO/CPO momentum. We see strategic rationale, although surprised about timing ahead of key ramps. Scarcity value of assets a positive for COHR; see more as a headwind for CIEN longer term.   
---  
  
What was announced. Following last week's Bloomberg report, Marvell (covered
by Joe Moore) and Lumentum announced a definitive agreement on Monday,
November 2, under which MRVL will acquire LITE in an all-stock transaction
(see ourfirst-take
note).
LITE shareholders will receive 4.5 MRVL shares for each LITE share, implying a
transaction enterprise value of approximately $115bn, or $1,132 per LITE
share, and a 23.9% premium to unaffected October 28 price. MRVL and LITE
shareholders will own approximately 67% and 33% of the combined company,
respectively, on a fully diluted basis. Management expects the transaction to
close in 1H CY28, with Matt Murphy remaining CEO and Chairman and three LITE
directors, including CEO Michael Hurlston, joining MRVL's board. MRVL expects
more than $1bn in annual run-rate cost synergies, primarily from COGS, and
non-GAAP EPS accretion in the first year following closing. Management expects
a 1H CY28 close, with potential regulatory extensions through August 2028. We
do not see another buyer given the size of the transaction.

Our initial perspective remains largely unchanged, with the transaction
highlighting the strategic importance of optical technology and manufacturing
capacity. We see rationale in combining MRVL's optical DSPs, switching and
connectivity solutions with LITE's laser technology, InP manufacturing assets
and growing NPO/CPO and OCS opportunities. LITE's recent earnings momentum and
>$5bn in NPO/CPO commitments further highlight the value of its assets, though
the sold out conditions through FY28 leave little unknown. Given deal approval
not expected until the 1H'CY28, focus in the interim to be around ramping OCS
/ CPO capacity to be able to hit >$5bn targets.

Read-through to our coverage – supply tightness likely to persist, with mixed
implications for COHR. For CIEN, LITE is a key component supplier for pump
lasers and narrow line width lasers. While some of that bottleneck should
clear over the next year and a half during the approval process, MRVL is a
major competitor to CIEN on the ZR pluggables side, making relying on a
competitor for supply of key products awkward (similar dynamics existed for
NOK / Infinera when Acacia was acquired by Cisco). For COHR, from a strategic
perspective, the transaction further validates the importance and scarcity
value of COHR's optical technology and manufacturing assets. This is offset by
competitive dynamics on transceivers. We also don't have a sense of how much
MRVL would like to get the transceiver assembly business, but definitely
consolidates more of the BOM of a transceiver with one vendor, a headwind for
the space.

F1Q27 margin upside, a second major NPO/CPO win and strong F2Q guidance. LITE
reported revenue of $1.263bn (+25.5% Q/Q), ~0.6% above consensus but below the
~$1.28bn buyside bogey. Non-GAAP GM of 53.2% was ~170bps above consensus and
in line with buyside expectations, while operating margin of 42.3% was ~250bps
above consensus and ahead of the ~41% buyside bogey. EPS of $4.57 was ~9%
above consensus and ahead of buyside expectations of $4.40-$4.45. Key
incremental disclosure was a second major NPO/CPO win backed by >$5bn in
purchase commitments, providing further validation of customer demand for
next-generation optical scale-up architectures (though we would note the
company had already alluded to this in media appearances during the quarter).
Management also highlighted pump lasers and OCS as the leading growth
contributors, with significantly improved OCS demand visibility supporting the
potential for a multi-billion-dollar annual revenue stream. For F2Q, revenue
guidance of $1.60bn was ~7% above consensus and at the high end of the
$1.55bn-$1.60bn bogeys, implying ~$350mm of sequential growth. EPS guidance of
$6.05 was ~19% above consensus, with non-GAAP operating margin guidance of
45-46% pointing to another ~270-370bps of sequential expansion as the business
continues to scale. Read

# Apple

## F4Q26 Review: Pricing Power Drives Hardware Upside, But Services Moderation
& Memory Headwinds Temper Earnings; Reiterate OW

  
---  
  
By Samik Chatterjee, CFA
AC,
Jaiden R
Patel,
Mashu
Nishi

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
AAPL, AAPL US  
Price (02 Nov 26):$338.32  
**▼** Price Target (Dec-27):$355.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$360.00  
  
The primary discussion around AAPL shares following the earnings print will
likely be around the changing trajectory of Hardware vs. Services growth,
where despite the concerns around supply constraints as well as price
elasticity following significant price increases, Product (and iPhone)
revenues have delivered to expectations, while on the flip-side we have seen a
steady moderation in the growth rate for Services, which is increasingly going
to call into question the long-term Services growth rate when faced with
mobile gaming headwinds, app store business model changes and 3P licensing
(i.e. including Google in our view) headwinds. On the Services front, we
believe Apple is still in the early days in relation to the roll-out of the
revamped Siri AI which will lay the groundwork for its opportunity with
monetizing services with the installed base, that reached a record over 2.5B
devices, and will likely evolve to keep abreast with the industry’s move
towards consumer agents in time; in the meantime, before the incremental
monetization drivers start to contribute meaningfully, we might be in a
relatively new phase for the company wherein Hardware is the driver of growth
in revenue and earnings with the launch of a refreshed line up of new devices
across iPhones, iPads, and Macs positioned to support the sustainability of
the robust revenue growth demonstrated recently. On the hardware front,
positives included the iPhone revenue beat in F4Q despite supply chain
constraints as well as moderating processor-related constraints into F1Q, and
improving supply ramp on Duo - although visibility into timing of meeting
demand remains less clear at this time. Following the print, we are raising
our Product revenue forecasts for FY27 with the large majority of the upward
revisions led by Mac, iPad and stronger pricing outcomes on iPhone revenues,
while our Services revenue growth outlook as well as company gross margins
moderate on the combination of challenging gross margin mix (lower revenue
growth for high-margin Services relative to higher revenue growth for lower-
margin Products) as well as headwinds to both Services and Products gross
margins on a stand-alone basis; the net effect of which leads to lower
earnings forecasts for the company. However, the positive drivers of a
stronger hardware product cycle will lead to a stronger growth outlook for the
installed base, which drives the opportunity for a recovery in the Services
growth trajectory through a broadening of offerings and across geographies,
overcoming the near-term headwinds. We are reiterating our Overweight rating
on the shares long-term with the strength of the hardware product cycle
enabling Apple to steadily deliver to a Services opportunity in line with
investor expectations as it continues to roll-out and further refine its
innovation associated with Siri AI in conjunction with the related
monetization.

  * F4Q26 (Sep-end) Results: EPS beat relative to consensus driven by better revenues and gross margins, along with a lower tax rate. Revenues tracked to $114.5B (+12% y/y) vs. JPMe of $112.9B and consensus of $113.5B, with the revenue beat relative to consensus driven by iPhone and Mac, offset to some extent by iPad and Wearables, Home and Accessories. iPhone revenues tracked to $57.6B or +17% y/y (vs. JPMe of $56.0B and consensus of $56.5B), while Services tracked to $31.6B (vs. JPMe of $31.5B and consensus of $31.6B) or a growth of +10% y/y, which is largely in-line with management guide. Gross margins tracked to 47.9% (vs. JPMe of 47.4% and consensus of 47.6%), including an ~100 bps benefit from tariff refunds as guided, with Product margin of 37.2% (vs. JPMe of 36.5% and consensus of 36.9%) and Services margin of 76.0% (vs. JPMe of 75.6% and consensus of 75.1%). Opex came in at $19.2B, in line with both JPMe and consensus. EPS tracked to $2.10 vs. JPMe of $1.96 and consensus of $2.00, including a 5c benefit from tariff refunds and a lower tax rate of 15.0% (vs. JPMe of 17.5%).
  * F1Q27 (Dec-end) Guidance: Revenue upside relative to consensus, offset by memory-led gross margin headwinds and higher opex. The company guided total revenue growth of +7-10% y/y, which is well above JPMe of +3% y/y and consensus of +6% y/y, despite constrained supply and on top of +16% y/y growth in the prior year, while Services growth is guided to +8-9% y/y (vs. JPMe of +13% y/y and consensus of +12% y/y) on account of headwinds from third-party licensing and FX. Gross margins are guided to a range of 45.0%-46.0% (vs. JPMe and consensus of 46.7%), representing a ~140 bps q/q decline at the midpoint from the adjusted F4Q26 level of 46.9% excluding tariff refunds, with management indicating that most of the decline is driven by higher memory costs, along with costs related to the ramp of Siri AI. Opex is guided to $20.4-$20.8B (vs. JPMe/consensus of $20.3B/$19.9B), reflecting continued investments in AI, which in aggregate implies EPS broadly in line with consensus expectations heading into the print.
  * Memory headwinds to persist beyond the Dec-Q, with supply constraints shifting to Mac and iPad. Management characterized memory pricing as unprecedented and expects memory costs to continue to increase beyond the Dec-Q, with a decreasing benefit from carrying inventory over time. While constraints on advanced nodes are easing with the transition to 2nm, the company expects constraints on Mac and iPad in the Dec-Q driven by memory, while iPhone Duo remains constrained with limited visibility into supply-demand balance.

Apple beat on iPhone and Mac revenue, but slower Services growth and margin
pressure temper FY27. We raise our price target to $340.  
|  |  | Global Research   
02 November 2026  
---|---|---  
| Apple Inc.| ●| (AAPL.O) Neutral|  
---|---|---|---  
| Growth and margins should downtick in fiscal
2027  
---  
| Apple beat on iPhone and Mac revenue, but slower Services growth and margin
pressure temper FY27. We raise our price target to $340.  
  
| | Read Report   > |   
---|---  
| **Gross margin should compress in FY27 following Services driven expansion
the past several years**  
---  

  
Source: Company data and UBS estimates  
| Slowing Services, GM pressure & limited AI traction offset iPhone demand
Apple reported a broadly in-line quarter
(link),
with iPhone and Mac strength offset by supply-constrained iPad results, weaker
Wearables and in-line Services. Investor attention should turn to December-
quarter gross margin guidance of 45% to 46%, below our already below-consensus
estimates, and expected Services revenue growth of 8% to 9% as AI tools appear
to cannibalize Google search activity QoQ. Although a one- or two-percentage-
point revenue growth slowdown has little impact on EPS, it will likely weigh
disproportionately on Apple's valuation multiples. Services has contributed
disproportionately to growth and gross margin, with its share of total revenue
rising from ~20% in fiscal 2022 to ~26% in fiscal 2026. With incremental Siri
AI ramp costs weighing on December-quarter margins and Apple's AI strategy
still appearing nascent, particularly in agentic tools, we expect its P/E
multiple to compress to ~31x from 36x. Q4:26 Highlights:

  1. iPhone rev of $57.6 billion, up ~18% YoY, was ~3% above our $56.0 billion estimate but slowed from low 20s% growth in the past three quarters. Checks suggested better China demand (Greater China revenue +21% YoY) and strength in the base 17 series before the launch of the 18 Pro/Max models likely drove the modest upside.
  2. Services rev of $31.6B or ~10% YoY growth (guide ~10%) was in-line with our $31.6B estimate. The guide for FQ1 is growth of 8%-9% (incl. 50bps of incremental f/x pressure), which is below our prior est. of 11.5%. 
  3. Gross margin of 47.9% was slightly above our 47.5% estimate (guide 47% to 48%) as we est a tariff refund was roughly a ~100 bps tailwind. Ex the tariff benefit, we estimate GM was down ~30 bps YoY. The guide for FQ1 is 45%-46% vs our prior 45.9% (cons. 46.6%) as memory and ramp costs associated with Siri AI weigh. 
  4. Normalizing EPS for tariff and a lower tax rate, diluted EPS would be roughly $2.00 vs $1.85 a year ago or ~8% like-for-like growth.
  5. Mac rev was strong, up 24% YoY to $10.8B vs our $9.4B despite ongoing supply constraints. 

Adjust estimates by a few pennies We slightly tweak our FY27 and FY28 EPS
estimates to $9.55 and $10.56 from $9.58 and $10.54 respectively.Increase our
PT to $340 from $296 as we roll to CY28 and nudge mult higher to 31x We
increase our Apple price target to $340 as we roll to CY28 EPS estimate of
$10.83 vs our prior 50/50 weighting of CY27/CY28 ($10.32) and nudge our target
multiple to 31x from 29x, in-line with the trailing 1 and 3-year averages.
Although growth is slowing, Apple's multiple is likely to be resilient in the
near-term as the market rotates away from AI infrastructure exposed companies.
That said, gross margin pressure and decelerating Services growth are dynamics
that the market will closely scrutinize on our view.December outlooks reflects
more modest demand and higher costs

  * Apple expects December-quarter revenue growth of 7% to 10%, implying $153.8 billion to $158.1 billion, versus our $153.4 billion estimate (+6.7%) and Visible Alpha consensus of $153.1 billion (+6.5%).
    * Although Apple did not specify December-quarter iPhone revenue growth, we raise our forecast to 11.5%, reflecting pricing and a mix shift toward Duo.
    * Apple expects Services revenue growth of 8% to 9% year-over-year, below both our estimate and Visible Alpha consensus of 11.6%. Slower App Store growth and Search pressure, foreshadowed by Alphabet’s results, should drive roughly 500 bps of year-over-year growth deceleration.
  * Gross margin guidance of 45% to 46% aligns with our preview (link), as tariff tailwinds fade and Apple absorbs materially higher memory costs. Select iPhone and Mac price increases announced in recent months partially offset these pressures. Foreign exchange will reduce gross margin by 50 bps, with additional Siri AI ramp costs also weighing on margins.
  * Operating expenses to be between $20.4B and $20.8B.
  * OI&E expected to be $300M and Tax Rate expected 17%. 

Margin gains lifted valuation, but fiscal 2027 presents downside risk

  * Services supported multiple expansion: Services’ share of Apple’s consolidated revenue rose from 22% in fiscal 2023 to roughly 26% in fiscal 2026, while its gross margin increased roughly 500 bps, from ~71% to ~76% (figure 1). We view these margin gains as the main driver of Apple’s NTM P/E expansion from ~27x to ~36x (figure 2).
  * December-quarter gross margin guidance declines year-over-year: Apple projects 45% to 46%, versus 48.2% a year earlier, as higher component costs, including DRAM and NAND, weigh on Product gross margin.
  * Fiscal 2027 gross margin likely declines year-over-year: With component costs elevated and tariff tailwinds absent, we forecast consolidated gross margin of 47.2%, down roughly 160 bps. We therefore expect Apple’s NTM P/E to fall from ~36x, a premium of over 80%, to ~31x, a premium of ~60%. That multiple would be below its fiscal 2024 and 2025 levels, when gross margin was 46% to 47%, versus the 45% to 46% guide for fiscal 2027.

We make minor changes to our ests but revenue and margin bias is lower
Reflecting our latest round of post quarter checks and management's
commentary, we make minor changes to our Apple estimates. While the outlook is
largely unchanged, we note there could be downside bias to our flattish iPhone
unit forecast and assumption that Mac takes material share as the markets
decline of 6% in calendar 2027. Finally, our fiscal 2027 gross margin forecast
of 47.2% (prior ~47% and Visible Alpha consensus 47.4%) could also experience
downward pressure given supply chain component shortages and persistent
elevated DRAM and NAND prices.iPhone revenue grew ~18% YoY driven by ASP
increases

  * September qtr performance: iPhone revenue came in at $57.6B, topping our $56.0B estimate by ~3% (VA Cons $56.4B). Revenue grew ~18% year-over-year, following three consecutive quarters of growth above 20%. Checks indicate the 17 series was well received driven by a refresh cycle while supply availability partly supported Apple’s share gains in markets such as China. As such, we estimate pricing adjustments accounted for about 80% of the iPhone revenue growth in the quarter while units were up low single digits.
  * December qtr outlook: Supply chain checks and recent sell-through data suggest demand is softening as the latest refresh cycle wanes. Therefore, we forecast iPhone revenue growth of ~11.5% driven by price as initial Duo demand and recent price increases offset softening demand for the legacy 17 base model ahead of the expected 18 launch in the March-27 quarter..
  * Fiscal 2027: We expect roughly flat iPhone unit growth in fiscal 2027, given supply chain disruption risks and evidence that recent strength may have pulled demand forward. A mix shift toward ~11 million Duo units and recent price increases support our ASP forecast of $1,072, up roughly 10% year-over-year. These assumptions underpin our updated iPhone revenue forecast of $281.4 billion, up 10.7% YoY (prior $277.5 billion / Visible Alpha Cons $276.8 billion).

Macs pick up share while iPad faced a tough comp Against a tough PC backdrop,
Mac revenue came in at $10.8B up ~24% YoY vs our $9.4B (VA Cons $9.6B) as
supply availability, although constrained, has driven share gains relative to
Dell, HP, and Lenovo. On the other hand, iPad revenue came in at $6.2B, down
~10% YoY missing our $6.6B estimate and the Visible Alpha consensus of
~$7.0BServices growth remains stuck in neutral. Sub 10% growth is a first
Services revenue came in at $31.6B, up 10% year-over-year vs our $31.6B
estimate. For the December quarter, Apple noted it expects Services growth of
8% to 9% as headwinds in its third party licensing business (Google)
decelerates as expected. Therefore, we trim our December quarter Services
revenue forecast to $32.6B or up 8.7% year-over-year (prior $33.5B / 11.6%).
High-single digit Services revenue growth is not only a gross margin headwind
but in our view, should put pressure on Apple's P/E multiple as the mix shift
has been a key contributor to multiple expansion the past five years.AI
concerns and gross margins influence valuation; we raise our target multiple
from 29x to 31x and price target from $296 to $340 Apple shares gained roughly
9% over the past three months despite mixed June-quarter results,
substantially outperforming declines of ~3% in the S&P 500 and 12% in SMH. We
view SMH, the semiconductor index, as a proxy for AI infrastructure sentiment.
As discussed earlier, a higher Services revenue mix supported gross margin
expansion and drove Apple’s NTM P/E to roughly 36x, an ~80% premium to the S&P
500, versus expected calendar 2027 EPS growth of ~9%.Although an 80% premium
is hard to justify given modest expected EPS growth and gross margin risk, we
raise our Apple price target by rolling forward to calendar 2028 EPS estimates
from the previous 50/50 weighting of 2027 and 2028. We also increase our
target multiple from 29x to 31x, consistent with the trailing 1- and 3-year
averages. At 31x, Apple would trade at roughly a 60% premium to the S&P 500
NTM P/E, slightly more than 1 standard deviation above its trailing 3- and
5-year average premiums. Despite modest growth and a far-from-robust AI
strategy, Apple’s strong balance sheet and low capital intensity (roughly 2%
of revenue) are likely to command a premium, particularly amid market
financing concerns and widening credit spreads over the past three months.

messages.subject: IDEA: Marvell Technology Group Ltd: MRVL/LITE deal - an aggressive move with significant potential
messages.body_excerpt:
| | | |   
---  
  
---  
| | |   
---  
Marvell Technology Group Ltd (MRVL.O)  
MRVL/LITE deal - an aggressive move with significant potential  
| | Read Full Report  
---  
(PDF: 17 Pages)  
---  
| North America  
---  
Stock Rating   Equal-weight  
Price Target   $300.00  
Joseph Moore, Meta A Marshall, Ella Tulchinsky, Mason Wayne, Shane Brett,
Nicole Kozhukhov & 1 more...  
November 3, 2026  
---  
| | | The deal brings risks but also opportunities; the company's very strong track record with M&A gives us comfort, and the selloff in the stock seems overdone.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * The benefits of co designing lasers and electronics for next generation optics seem clear 
  * That said, laser margins are potentially more cyclical than base MRVL, and some of MRVL's DSP customers are Lumentum competitors 
  * The $1 bn in synergy - mostly COGS - is non trivial and will take time to play out 
  * Marvell's strong track record with M&A is a positive precedent, with Cavium, Inphi, and Avera all exceeding revenue and cost synergy targets 

  
  
Our view: Marvell has a strong record of buying into technology inflections
and successfully retaining key talent and driving accelerated growth, and we
see the potential that the Lumentum (covered by Meta Marshall) deal follows
the same playbook. Inphi is the clearest precedent. It looked expensive at
announcement and Marvell’s shares fell afterward, but that business is on
track to have grown more than 10x since. The bar is higher here. At $115bn of
enterprise value, the deal is more than 10x the size of Inphi and the largest
semiconductor acquisition ever agreed. Cavium and Avera are also deals where
Marvell exceeded all cost and revenue synergy targets, all of which gives us
some comfort around a deal that certainly will require strong execution.

We see the benefits of co-designing lasers and electronics for next-generation
optics, which is the core of the strategic case. In scale-up, customers are
already asking for integrated solutions from a single supplier. The $1bn+ run-
rate cost synergy target, primarily COGS, comes from pulling each company’s
content into the solutions the other already sells to customers. The
opportunity should grow with revenue and, over time, with co-optimized
roadmaps. However, delivering the synergies depends on Marvell winning that
content without pushing competing module makers toward other DSP suppliers.

We also see two broader risks. Lumentum is earning margins above its own
target model on tight InP supply, and the valuation assumes those economics
hold well beyond a 1H28 close. The deal also needs Chinese approval, and
China-based module makers, which buy Marvell’s DSPs and compete with Lumentum,
account for most transceiver supply. The strategic logic is sound, but the
price leaves little room for error.

Deal Summary

Marvell will acquire Lumentum in an all stock transaction at a fixed exchange
ratio of 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. The deal implies
approximately $115 billion of enterprise value, or roughly $1,132 per Lumentum
share, representing a 23.9% premium to Lumentum’s unaffected October 28
closing price. Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined
company, with Lumentum shareholders owning approximately 33%. Closing is
expected in the first half of calendar 2028.

Marvell highlights a combined 2030 TAM of $550 billion, more than $1 billion
of annual run rate cost synergies, and expected accretion to non GAAP EPS in
year one post close.

Strategic Rational

Our view is that the deal has a strong technology basis in scale-up and scale-
in, where future optical architectures will require lasers and electronics to
be co-designed. In today’s scale-out market, the combination creates an
opportunity to pull each company’s content into the other’s products, but is
also a risk to Marvell’s position as a neutral supplier.

Lumentum brings hard-to-replicate InP laser, optical switching and
manufacturing capabilities, while Marvell brings the switches, NPO products,
DSPs and custom silicon. Together, the companies can co-design light sources
and optical engines directly into the switch and XPU, improving performance,
reducing qualification time and potentially increasing content per link.
Lumentum’s current positions support this case. It leads in 200G EMLs used in
1.6T pluggables and holds 70-80% share in pump lasers. In optical switching,
it is the leading merchant OCS supplier and has a multiyear, multi-billion-
dollar OCS agreement. In CPO, it supplies UHP lasers into Nvidia’s switches,
and Nvidia invested $2 billion in Lumentum alongside a multibillion-dollar
purchase commitment. Lumentum also announced today its second major NPO/CPO
win, which management expects to generate over $5 billion of revenue with
shipments starting in 2H CY27.

Why not just partner? A partnership could have captured some of the technology
benefits at a much lower cost, particularly because Marvell and Lumentum
already collaborate across parts of the optical stack. The counterargument is
that scale-up changes the model. In scale-out, customers can qualify a switch
and module from separate suppliers, while in scale-up the switch, optical
engine and light source need to be co-designed with shared roadmaps and
tighter systems integration. Ownership also secures priority access to scarce
InP capacity to support growth.

On the opportunity side, management expects more than $1bn of annual run-rate
synergies, primarily from COGS, by pulling each company’s content into the
other’s products, and expects the synergies to grow as the combined company
scales. These savings come where one company’s content is not used today, for
example a Lumentum module built with another vendor’s DSP. Replacing a third-
party supplier captures that supplier’s margin and is a real saving. However,
Lumentum is already a big customer of Marvell. Those existing sales are
eliminated in consolidation and add no earnings, and they also shrink the pool
of third-party content left to replace. Management did not provide detail on
the split of the $1bn and did not quantify opex synergies. We assume none
near-term given the employee base needed to support growth. No revenue
synergies were quantified. Over time, co-designed scale-up engines using
internal lasers and DSPs should carry structurally lower COGS, which we view
as margin on new revenue rather than a synergy against today’s cost base.
Despite limited information, this is an area where management's track record
gives us optimism.

In our view, the main scale-out risk is supplier neutrality. Marvell already
supplies DSPs and analog components to module makers that compete with
Lumentum, which creates a real supplier neutrality risk and could encourage
customers to shift DSP volume to other suppliers. Marvell is the leader in
merchant PAM4 DSPs, so even modest share loss at competing module makers would
matter. That said, management indicated it would continue selling components
across the entire ecosystem. Marvell already sells its own DCI modules while
supplying coherent DSPs to competing module makers, and Lumentum already sells
lasers to most of its module competitors. Management also said module makers
have expressed support since the announcement. We find these precedents
encouraging but not conclusive. DCI is a much smaller market than scale-out
PAM4, and Lumentum’s laser customers have had few alternatives while capacity
is tight. The clearest evidence will be next-generation DSP design wins, which
module makers will award during the deal’s pendency.

|  Source: Company
Presentation  
---  
 Source: Company
Presentation  
---  
  
Pro Forma Model

Based on Marvell’s FQ3’27 guidance and Lumentum’s FQ1’27 results, the combined
company would have $17.7 billion of annualized revenue, a 57% non GAAP gross
margin and a 39% operating margin before synergies. The company also points to
more than $1 billion of annual run rate synergies, primarily from COGS, and
expects the transaction to be accretive to gross margin, operating margin and
EPS in the first year after close. This is a current run rate snapshot rather
than a forecast for the first full year, so we build our own CY29 pro forma
below.

MRVL Pro Forma Snapshot  
---  
 Source: Company
Presentation  
---  
  
Our model: Assuming the transaction closes during CY28, we use CY29 as the
first full calendar year in our pro forma analysis. We model approximately
$71.0 billion of revenue, $41.1 billion of gross profit, a 57.8% gross margin,
a 46.8% operating margin and $20.27 of pro forma non GAAP EPS. Our CY29 pro
forma includes $700 million of COGS synergies but no operating expense or
revenue synergies.

Against CY29 consensus EPS of $19.76, our pro forma is approximately 3%
accretive. Given how far out the transaction is, the range of estimation error
is wide. The outcome will depend on company performance, how quickly synergies
are realized and when the deal closes. Our standalone Marvell CY29 EPS
estimate is $21.55, above consensus, so the deal is slightly dilutive based on
our higher estimates for MRVL, but we would agree that there is accretion
potential vs. consensus.

 Source: Morgan Stanley
Research  
Note: CY2027E standalone figures are Morgan Stanley Research estimates for
each company on a calendar-year, non-GAAP basis (Marvell fiscal year ends
January; Lumentum fiscal year ends June).  
CY2029E pro forma reflects the first full year following the expected 1H
CY2028 close; all-stock consideration of 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share.  
Includes COGS synergies of $700mm in CY2029E (company target: $1bn+ run-rate);
pro forma tax rate of 15%.  
---  
  
Other key considerations

Peak Laser Economics. Lumentum is already operating above its original target
model. Its March 2026 OFC framework called for a 49-52% gross margin and
38-42% operating margin at an $8 billion annualized revenue run rate. In
FQ1'27 it reported a 53.2% gross margin and 42.3% operating margin at a $5
billion run rate, and it guided to a 45-46% operating margin for FQ2'27.
Lumentum's gross margin has expanded by more than 2,000bp over the last eight
quarters, driven by pricing, 200G EML mix, pump laser pricing and fab
utilization. All incremental EML capacity is covered by long-term agreements
through CY27.

The risk is that Marvell is paying for scarcity economics that normalize
before closing or before new capacity is fully loaded. Lumentum's margins are
well above historical levels and could normalize through Chinese competition
or if more of the scale-up opportunity goes to VCSELs. Management argues that
supply tightness is a byproduct of a durable architectural shift, and that the
number of lasers required for scale-up and scale-in is massive. We agree the
architectural transition is real, but the valuation leaves limited room for a
slowdown in AI spending, pricing or utilization.

CPO and NPO timing. Lumentum's second major NPO and CPO win is an important
proof point. Management said timing is consistent with its largest CPO
customer, with shipments in 2H CY27, and that volume is high because the
customer's optical lane density is very high. Lumentum expects its first
scale-up CPO shipments by late CY27 and sizes the first phase of scale-up CPO
at 3-4x scale-out CPO. Most of the upside in this deal comes from these newer
opportunities and from more tightly integrated optics and electronics. The
deal isn't expected to close until 2028, but the timing of these next-
generation optical opportunities matters for the deal's value to be realized.

Capital intensity, cyclicality, and new management challenges. Lumentum adds a
more capital-intensive manufacturing model. Its capex was ~15% of revenue in
FY26, versus mid-to-high single digits for Marvell. Lumentum is running at
mid-teens and would normalize to ~10%. Lumentum's margins are influenced by
fab utilization, product mix, pricing and capacity additions. The company has
also indicated that a new fab can require approximately $650 million of
investment. Its Greensboro, NC fab, which begins ramping UHP lasers in 2028,
adds more than $5 billion of revenue capacity, per management. The opportunity
is attractive if demand remains structurally above supply, but the combined
company will carry more fixed-cost and working-capital risk if the cycle
turns.

Regulatory approval. The transaction requires approval in the United States
and China. Lumentum has noted that 60-65% of transceivers come from China-
based vendors. Any concern that Marvell could restrict DSP access or favor its
own modules could create pressure from customers or regulators. That said,
there is little overlap between the companies and management has indicated
that it received positive feedback from ecosystem partners, including in
China, and has allowed ample time to complete the process.

What the Price Requires

At $115 billion of enterprise value, Marvell is paying approximately 22x
Lumentum’s current annualized quarterly revenue and roughly 38x fiscal 2026
revenue. Historical optical acquisitions were generally completed at
approximately 2x to 11x LTM revenue, although most of those targets were
smaller and less exposed to AI infrastructure. The premium reflects Lumentum’s
growth, InP capacity and strategic scarcity, and it means the deal requires
substantial execution beyond combining two existing businesses.

We continue to model Marvell on a standalone basis given the long path to
closing. The deal is expected to close in 1H CY28, with an outside date that
can extend to August 2028, and requires shareholder approval at both companies
and regulatory approval in the US and China.

The strategic case is strongest if scale-up optics develop into a large
integrated market in which customers prefer one supplier across switches,
optical engines and light sources. Our bottom line is that the transaction is
strategically logical but financially demanding. The key proof point will be
whether Marvell and Lumentum can convert scale-up engagements into repeatable,
high-margin, co-designed platforms without losing Marvell’s DSP share at
competing module makers. The deal carries real execution risk, but Marvell’s
M&A track record gives us comfort, and we think the selloff in the stock is
overdone. Read

for MRVL.

| **Accretion Sensitivity Analysis for Various LITE EPS Assumptions**  
---  

  
Source: Company reports, UBS research, FactSet  
| What Happened This morning, MRVL announced
the acquisition of
LITE in an all-stock transaction valuing LITE at ~$115B EV / ~$1,132 per share
- effectively, a ~24% premium to unaffected prices prior to the deal reported
by various media outlets late last week
(here,
here). Upon
approval, LITE shareholders would receive 4.5 MRVL shares per share and will
own ~33% of the combined company. The deal combines MRVL's DSPs, TIAs/drivers,
switching, custom silicon, and SiPho with LITE's lasers, optical components,
OCS, and InP/GaAs manufacturing - effectively a move to vertically integrate.
The deal also adds ~$60B to the combined TAM, with most of this coming from
NPO/CPO. LITE also disclosed a second major NPO/CPO win expected to generate
>$5B of revenue, though in speaking with UBS analyst David Vogt, this is
already contemplated in investor bogeys for C2028. Management expects >$1B of
run-rate synergies, primarily from COGS/content pull-through, with GM/OpM and
non-GAAP EPS accretion beginning in year one. Closing is expected in 1H28.Pro-
Forma Merger Model Financially, if we were to use UBSe C2028 LITE EPS, our
pro-forma analysis suggests the deal to be marginally dilutive (~8%) to UBSe
C2028 MRVL EPS; however, we also see a scenario in which it could be ~14%
accretive if we were to consider where investor bogeys for LITE currently
stand. We think guidance for ~$1B in synergies, primarily from COGS, is
achievable. Finally, the all-stock transaction implies an enterprise value of
$115B for LITE and a ~33x C2028 P/E multiple. Our Take We like the deal for
MRVL, although we can certainly see how investors - especially LITE
shareholders - could question the timing and see this as potential indication
of peak-cycle/shortage. From MRVL’s perspective, we think this is all about
being able to move faster with fully integrated solutions - particularly for
scale-up and scale-in - by co-designing the electrical and optical pieces
rather than qualifying them separately. LITE's laser/InP capability is the key
missing piece for MRVL, including microVCSEL for scale-in connectivity into
the XPU package. There is also precedent for the companies working together:
MRVL and LITE demonstrated LITE's R300 OCS with multiple classes of modules
powered by MRVL optical DSPs at OFC 2026, so this is not a completely new
technical relationship. We understand the risk that MRVL is maybe buying
at/near peak optical conditions and inherits a more capital-intensive
manufacturing model, but this seems less about owning today's module revenue
and more about controlling the critical light-source technologies needed as
optics move progressively closer to compute in a future world. Based on UBS
LITE and MRVL estimates, we estimate the deal would be 8% dilutive to C2028
EPS, though we believe expectations among many LITE bulls are for EPS numbers
considerably higher than where the Street (or UBS) sits today. This is shown
in our pro-forma sensitivity table (Figure 2) and we conclude that in the LITE
bull case, the deal would actually be fully ~14% accretive to C2028,
potentially pushing MRVL’s EPS to the ~$15 range on a pro-forma basis. Read
Across

  * Increased competitive pressure for AVGO: We think MRVL+LITE creates a broader competitor to AVGO across AI connectivity by combining MRVL's DSP/SerDes, switching, custom silicon, and SiPho with LITE's InP/laser capabilities. The bigger question to us is whether another buyer could come over the top given the scarcity and strategic value of LITE's optical assets. We think it is possible that AVGO may want to double down on its asset portfolio, but there could also be anti-trust considerations. NVDA would seem maybe more likely to make a competing bid, though we have no evidence of such a development. 
  * Positive for merchant silicon / hyperscale relationships: Both MRVL and LITE have deep relationships with merchant silicon and hyperscaler providers, and the combination should create more opportunities to co-design scale-up/scale-in solutions and increase content. The companies believe the combination should strengthen rather than disrupt these existing partnerships, particularly in CPO, where MRVL adds Inphi and Celestial AI's SiPho capabilities to LITE's optical portfolio. LITE also announced a new NPO win expected to generate >$5B, though UBS LITE analyst David Vogt believes this is already reflected in investor expectations and our C28 pro forma EPS estimates.

Valuation: Our standalone MRVL estimates are unchanged and our price target
remains $350 (~28x C2028 EPS of $12.75).

  * This $10bn WNG bond deal and $10bn stock offering match the Analyst Day plan, but arrive sooner than expected and defy February's guide for no more CY26 bonds.

  * ORCL's cash walk implied tens of billions of potential 5Y vendor financing, which we expect to be less transparent and Moody's now confirms as debt-like. 
  * AMZN will grant a security interest in certain purchased assets in connection with its new up-to-$80bn facility, with principal repayments outside FCF. A similar ORCL structure could prime unsecureds, warranting attention to a potential ~20% priority threshold for unsecured/CFR rating parity, as we flagged last year. 
  * Supplier financing is drawing scrutiny – but also interest as a capital source – across IG and LevFin investors. Near-term DELL spread pressure feels warranted pending clarity.

index debt amount will exceed $125bn but prudently remain well below bank
levels. Still, today's related deal is not a clearing event in our view.

credit risks. The favorable technicals from limited further ORCL AI infra-

ecosystem supply. We remain medium-term cautious, albeit with less conviction

**UBS TECH / Earnings Previews:****AAPL, ON, PLTR, DOCN, DT, ALAB, AMD, ANET,

**AAPL****(11/2 AMC, Conf Call 5pm) ~3.96% Impl Vol / 6.5/10 Sentiment. David
Vogt previewed and b ased on supply chain checks, our analysis of smartphone
industry sell-through data
(****link****)
and wait time data (****link****),
he fine-tune our Apple estimates ahead of earnings but limited changes**. Our
September-quarter revenue and diluted EPS estimates are effectively unchanged,
while we make minor adjustments to our fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenue and EPS
forecasts as initial Duo demand strength was already reflected in our Apple
estimates. For the September quarter:**** We expect Apple to report
**September-quarter iPhone revenue of $56.0 billion** (prior: $55.9 billion)
and **total revenue of $112.8 billion** (prior: $112.7 billion), broadly in
line with our forecasts and compared with Visible Alpha consensus estimates of
$56.2 billion and $113.6 billion, respectively.** Our iPhone revenue forecast
is a touch below consensus, reflecting roughly 5% fewer units as checks point
to more muted near-term demand**, partly offset by blended ASPs that are about
5% higher due to product/variant mix and recent price increases. We therefore
expect iPhone revenue to grow ~14% year over year, a deceleration from 22% to
23% growth in each of the prior three quarters.**** We forecast **Services
revenue of $31.6 billion** , unchanged and just below the Visible Alpha
consensus of $31.7 billion. This implies year-over-year growth of 10%, a
roughly 200 bps sequential deceleration, as we estimate key categories such as
the App Store posted low single digit growth
(**link**)
during the quarter, ~800 bps slower than the year ago quarter.**** We forecast
**gross margin of 47.5%** , unchanged and in line with the Visible Alpha
consensus. Our estimate includes an approximately 100 bps benefit from a
tariff refund but down from 50.1% in the June quarter, which included a 250
bps uplift from tariff refunds. _Excluding tariff effects from all periods_ ,
we forecast gross margin of 46.5%, down approximately 70 bps year over year
and 100 bps sequentially largely due to higher component (DRAM) costs.**** Our
revenue and gross margin forecast should drive **diluted EPS to $1.97 (unch)**
, versus the Visible Alpha consensus of $1.99. However, a few cents of upside
is possible if Apple tightens spending and operating expenses fall below our
approximately $19.4 billion estimate, or 17.2% of revenue, and toward the low
end of the $19.1 billion to $19.4 billion guidance range. That said, we don’t
expect a potential opex driven beat to be rewarded by investors.****

**  **

****

**  **

**  **

**ON****(11/2 AMC, Conf Call 5pm) ~9.58% Impl Vol / 6.75/10 Sentiment. Tim
Arcuri previewed and he estimates Sept Q revenue/EPS of $1.69B/$0.87 (vs
Street $1.70B/$0.88) as TXN's results provide a constructive read-through
while our alternative data suggests strengthening pricing within the channel**
(see here).
We estimate Sept Q gross margin of 41%, with ON previously indicating that a
further round of price increases was underway and would take several quarters
to fully layer in. Into **Dec Q, we estimate revenue/EPS of $1.71B/$0.93 (vs
Street $1.74B/$0.96) - up 1.1% Q/Q and 2.9% above seasonality as the upcycle
continues to materialize**. That said, we continue to **see little in the way
of estimate revisions following the recent Analyst day**. At its Analyst Day,
ON made a solid argument for DD annual revenue growth, with pockets of
excitement around Data Center and the newly introduced Embedded Power Platform
(EPP). However, the long-term model was only in-line with our preview, while
the unchanged gross margin target is harder to view as a win given the
significantly improved demand backdrop. **The revised Synaptics acquisition
should also be a meaningful focus**. While the all-cash structure lowers the
headline transaction value and accelerates EPS accretion, on our calculation
ON is effectively paying more than the original share exchange would imply at
current prices. **All in, the analog backdrop is improving, but we need
clearer evidence of ON-specific participation and execution**.****

**_Key topics for earnings_****:** 1) End market demand trends, particularly
Automotive by geography and signs of backlog replenishment; 2) Pricing
tailwinds, utilization and progress on Fab Right efforts supporting gross
margin recovery; 3) Data Center momentum and customer adoption of EPP
following Analyst Day; 4) More detail on the revised SYNA transaction,
including financing, accretion and manufacturing insourcing synergies; 5) SiC
pricing, China EV participation and inventory trends.





**  **

**  **

**PLTR****(11/2 AMC, Conf Call 5pm) ~12.3% Impl Vol / 8.5/10 Sentiment. Karl
Keirstead recently attended Palantir’s AIPCon customer/leadership event
outside SF, where he spoke with customers and had time with Palantir’s
management. Bottom line, our view of Palantir as the best AI enabler in the
market** (making frontier models/AI useful in large enterprises) was if
anything bolstered by these conversations and demand momentum seems robust.
**PLTR continues to say that demand materially exceeds its ability to meet it
and enterprise AI adoption remains early, arguing that LLM limitations in
precision, enterprise integration, and decision-making reinforce Palantir’s
opportunity** in operational AI, model fine-tuning, and sovereign AI, while
the company intends to limit FDE headcount growth and sees little risk from
the pending midterm elections. Customers highlighted deployments spanning
marketing, supply-chain optimization, and security with an emphasis on
operational decision-making, reported little competitive pressure from models
or other data-software vendors, and pointed to a deepening relationship
between Palantir and Nvidia around bridging LLMs with real-world enterprise AI
applications.In our view, **the 2027 FCF multiple of 51x (well below that of
Snowflake and Crowdstrike) is very attractive given the 90%+ growth profile
and demand trends and we remain Buy-rated.**Full
Report

  * ** _Setup_** : The stock has rallied +20% since Q2 with elevated expectations. Key debate is whether US Commercial revs can sustain hyperscaler growth after posting +149% y/y in Q2 with cons at +22.7% y/y as comparison become materially harder. Additionally, commentary on the competitive landscape vs key LLM and Hyperscalers will be closely monitored followed by US Govt contract visibility with revenue at $798m (-1.3% y/y) post the midterms and margin trajectory. Also, any additional color on the recently announced Sovereign AI deployments with a new wave of customer including L3Harris, NVDA, and others. 
  * **PLTR guided to** **FQ3 revs $2.16-2.164b** and Op Income of $1.292-1.296b; **F’26 revs to $8.15-8.158b** , Op Income of $4.889-4.897b with FCF $4.7b 

**  **

**DOCN****(11/3 BMO, Conf Call 8am) ~14% Impl Vol / 5.5/10 Sentiment. Radi
Sultan previews and following recent checks he offers final thoughts ahead of
DOCN's 3Q26 print on Nov 3rd. He is leaning increasingly constructive on the
stock setup but the key risk is lack of follow-through due to broader AI
infra/funding concerns** (can DOCN decouple from the neoclouds?). Most
investors we speak with are also positive on the setup for Q3 revs growth +
the updated 2027 growth outlook, but we think incremental color on the funding
outlook may be the bigger driver. Key points to watch for on the funding
outlook would be: **1) a reaffirming that DOCN still has incremental equipment
financing capacity** (the market is still "open"), **2) sizing the incremental
financing needed to fund the 2027 capacity** expansion, or **3) the capex per
MW of incremental 2027 capacity** (the key variable in the financing
question). We addressed DOCN's funding outlook with a detailed illustrative
funding analysis (see our deep dive
here)
and in **our base case concluded DOCN may need ~$4b of incremental capital
(equipment financing, debt, etc.) through mid-2029** to finance our assumed
expansion to ~300 MWs in 2029. We do think risk/reward in the stock is
becoming increasingly favorable with the stock trading at ~7x the midpoint of
our illustrative $10-16 of EPS exiting 2029 laid out in our framework note
here.
(Radi Sultan) Full Report

  * ** _Setup_****: On the numbers setup we think the bar for Q3 is high-30% revenue growth, implying ~$35m q/q revs, which looks doable** given we believe the 10 MWs in KC was likely near full utilization most of Q3 (KC alone could've driven ~$35m of q/q revs) and 15 MWs in Memphis appeared to be online in August. On the **FY27 guide we think investors are evenly split between expecting a raise to 60%+/65%+ growth. Given the recent pullback in the stock we think a raise to 60%+ may be enough** and most investors we speak with still expect FY27 revenue growth to ultimately land in the ~75-80% range (some a bit higher). We net out positive on the tactical setup into the print. ****

**  **

**  **

**DT****(11/3 BMO, Conf Call 8am) ~11.9% Impl Vol / 7.5/10 Sentiment. Radi
Sultan previews upcoming result and following recent checks he leans cautious
on the tactical setup and would use near-term weakness as buying
opportunity.** Radi caught up with 4 Dynatrace checks (2 partners + 2
customers) ahead of the F2Q27 print and came away leaning cautious on the
tactical setup into the print but still positive on the multi-year growth
opportunity and more recently around AI/agent observability (see our recent
AI observability/Arize deep dive).
**We thought our checks sounded generally in-line with last quarter and all
pointed to stable spend & practice growth outlooks** (both partners in-line
with their C3Q targets). **However, our checks did note that AI
observability/Arize was not yet moving the needle** (more of an FY28+ driver)
and one partner did note a few large deals ($1-2m of combined ACV) slipped out
of CQ3 into CQ4. With investor sentiment on Dynatrace having improved
materially over the past few months (the most in our coverage universe), **we
think the positioning setup into the quarter is less favorable**. However,
we'd use any tactical weakness as a buying opportunity. Longer-term, we like
the multi-year growth potential and our work suggested that Arize + AI
observability will be key to DT’s ability to drive high-teens c/c ARR growth
over the next few years (UBSe 19%/18%/19% in FY27-29). On DT's quarterly pre-
quiet period call, see our recap
here.

  * **_Setup_** : **The key focus will again be net new ARR (c/c) and we believe mid-$80m of F2Q27 net new ARR (c/c) is doable** (roughly +20% y/y) and may be enough for the stock to work, but we see limited upside beyond this as one partner we spoke with did note a few large deals ($1-2m of combined ACV) slipped out of CQ3 into CQ4. **The key risk is that the investor bogey may have drifted higher than this to high-$80m which seems tougher** given the more stable growth outlooks and check feedback we heard. We net out more cautious on the tactical setup into the print. (Radi Sultan) Full Report



**  **

**ALAB****(11/3 AMC, Conf Call 4:30pm) ~11.9% Impl Vol / 7/10 Sentiment. Tim
Arcuri previewed and he expects upside to consensus estimates for both 3Q and
4Q and are modestly raising our 4Q EPS estimate, largely reflecting slightly
lower near-term OpEx expectations**. For 4Q, we expect revenue to grow ~20%
Q/Q, while UBS’s global team expects Trainium 3 units to increase ~15% Q/Q,
from ~0.6-0.7MM to ~0.7-0.8MM**. At the same time, we are encouraged by ALAB’s
progress across the broader portfolio, which we discussed following OCP
(****here****).
In particular, we see Orion potentially addressing two distinct opportunities:
(1)** providing neoclouds and smaller-scale customers that may lack the
resources to develop fully customized networking architectures with a more
standardized rack-level solution; and**(2)** we believe Orion could provide
AWS with an alternative rack architecture designed around its specific
requirements, potentially competing with other available solutions, including,
in our view, offerings from MRVL. On OpEx, what stood out to us this quarter
was just how much ALAB was able to bring to market across the portfolio,
particularly Orion and its new optical components (TIAs and drivers), with the
underlying R&D having taken place earlier this year. This causes us to revisit
our outer-year OpEx assumptions, although we continue to believe that a more
meaningful expansion into optical will ultimately require greater investment
than currently embedded in consensus expectations. **Net, our 3Q revenue/EPS
estimates remain unchanged at $557MM/$1.21, while our 4Q revenue/EPS estimates
move to $668MM/$1.42**. Our C2028 revenue/EPS estimates move to $3,789MM/$7.36
from $4,007MM/$7.69, reflecting a more conservative overall revenue outlook
despite a broader opportunity for Scorpio X, with lower OpEx partially
offsetting the revenue impact even as we continue to account for investment
required to build out ALAB’s optical portfolio.****

**Key topics for earnings:** 1) Switching and retimers revenue ramp for new
generation products ; 2) Design wins/ content gains at hyperscalers beyond
announced programs with AWS, GCP, MSFT, 3) CXL adoption timing; 4) copper to
Optical transition timeline and ALAB positioning.****







**  **

**  **

**AMD****(11/3 AMC, Conf Call 5pm) ~7.49% Impl Vol / 8.75/10 Sentiment. Tim
Arcuri previewed and he sees FQ3 (Sept) revenue in the ~$13.1-13.3B range
(high-end of guidance) and see AMD guiding FQ4 revenue potentially as high as
$17B (Street ~$16.2B) – a level broadly consistent with what we hear from
investors.** We see upside coming almost wholly from data center and

$142,371MM/$27.85 to $97,922MM/$17.58 and $139,993MM/$26.94.****

**Key topics for earnings:** 1) Server CPU demand trends near-term and longer-
term; 2) Helios MI455X revenue ramp; 3) Server CPU share expectations relative

accelerator shipments restrictions; 6) PC trends, TAM and share expectations

Friday was a brutal end to a rough week, with the SOX down -7.2% (now -19.1%
off of early Oct highs), led lower by INTC (and PC-related, especially DELL
and AMD) and MRVL (in part on equity-funded M&A reports with LITE); SNDK
(-13.5%) was also hit on fall-out from the Kioxia print. Neoclouds were also
hard hit. Industrial (GNRC, GEV, VRT potentially also including APH) and core
AI (NVDA, SMCI, GLW, JBL, MU) held up better, but were all down 3~6% as well.
JPM Pure Beta was down 5.6% and TMT Long-Short beta fell 7.4% (momentum held
up much better relative).



From my colleague Ilan Benhamou:



  
_JP Morgan_



The magnitude of Friday’s pullback was shocking – and I did not expect it –
but it’s not out of line with the marketing feedback I’ve been sharing over
the past month. I opened my October 18 Weekend note: “Much has already been
written about the recent, painful NDX/SOX pullback (The SOX is down -15.5%
over two weeks), though based on marketing feedback from recent visits with
Gokul Hariharan, Joe Cardoso and (this week) Harlan Sur, it’s not a surprise,
and even once the market catches a bid it’s unclear that Semis/AI will lead
the recovery.” And I opened our Oct 23 Specialist Delivery call by
underscoring: “Investors voiced … concerns loudly in recent dinners, lunches
and marketing events, and sentiment has been overwhelmingly bearish...”



I could say that INTC is likely idiosyncratic, and that in our opinion SNDK
actually sounded good last Thursday night, and instead blame the neoclouds and
CSP results; but that would be to deny the very real investor concerns about
power/shell and funding, with specific concerns broadly set around:



  1. **Will fixed income markets continue to provide capital for the AI buildout.** We’ve spoken _ad nauseum_ about this, including two all-hands calls with KOLs from across our CDS and fixed income teams; they so far haven’t seemed very worried (though with nuance, especially around neoclouds and HY issuance demand): “The underlying fundamentals and construction performance of projects, hyperscalers and the ecosystem in totality have been quite strong. Much of the negative narrative has been around continued investor willingness to lend and the total quantum of credit ultimately available to the space. We continue to think overall capacity is available.” The variable that most worries them is the signal from equity markets (“equity issuance reduces the technical overhang in credit”) so we’ll be keeping a close eye on any changes in view.****
  2. **Will private equity continue to fund AI capex?** Folks continue pointing to this week’s comments from Blackstone President Jon Gray that AI-related exposure is ~7% of the portfolio, as well as the report that AVGO CEO Hock Tan was deeply involved in negotiations to get parties to commit to fund XPV -  including helping banks get “more comfort around the guarantees from Broadcom that will protect them.” This wasn't the only disappointing news in privates late last week. 
  3. **Will equity markets support the build?** (This was a particular concern later in the week as folks started to call into question the ability of listed companies to maintain credit ratings and to borrow). There also remain concerns about where value accrues (to the labs?) 
  4. **Who will pay the bills to warehouse idle chips/components in case of delays in capacity build?**
  5. **Could Democratic victories gubernatorial elections – particularly in Texas and Nevada - derail the AI build?** And do we get a bounce on Wednesday if we avoid strong anti-data center mandates (or does the focus just shift to power availability, ’28 capex and rising costs)? We are positive on the setup for Arista shares heading into the 3Q26 print
with the stock down -14% since 2Q26 earnings (vs. -14% for AI peers and -2%
for S&P 500), amid concerns about the durability of the AI infrastructure
buildout, Arista’s exposure to hyperscaler and AI Lab customers, and the
possibility of conservative initial 2027 guidance given management’s typical
prudence and ongoing supply tightness. In our view, that caution creates a
favorable setup with intra-quarter revisions to end-market forecasts (see
industry model report
here) and hyperscaler capex outlooks (see cloud capex report
here) remaining supportive, large customer ramps on the horizon,
including Google and AI Lab customers, and scale-across and scale-up
opportunities layering onto a growing scale-out business. Notably, our review
of Arista’s prior 3Q guidance practices suggests the company has increasingly
set its initial full-year revenue outlook near consensus, then delivered
upside as the year progressed. With consensus currently forecasting revenue
growth of +29% y/y in 2027, we see +30% as a reasonable starting point that
investors would likely receive neutrally to positively based on our
discussions, while an outlook of +35% (or greater) would likely be received
more favorably. Importantly, we see a path to that higher starting figure,
even under conservative 2027 scenarios (see below), with sources of upside to
raise the outlook through the year including Arista’s share of hyperscaler
capex, which we forecast to grow close to +70% in 2027, the opportunity
associated with leading AI Lab customer deployments, and stronger growth
across the rest of the business, including DCI/scale-across, enterprise DC and
campus switching, as well as scale-up. We expect Arista’s updated TAM to also
reinforce the aforementioned, as we estimate it reaching $340 bn+ by 2030 vs.
$105 bn for 2029 issued in September 2025, implying a 30%+ CAGR over the
remainder of the decade. That could also set the stage for an upgrade to
Arista’s three-year revenue growth target, which it raised to 20%+ from the
mid-teens in May. Net-net, we are constructive heading into the print as we
expect a 3Q26 beat and a raise, accompanied by favorable 2027 initial
guidance, and the eventual step-up in the long-term growth expectations.
Reiterate Overweight.

  * 3Q26 Results: Revenue, margins and EPS to track ahead of JPMe, consensus, and guidance. JPMe forecasts revenue of $3.30 bn versus consensus of $3.33 bn and management guidance of approximately $3.30 bn. JPMe operating margin of 48.3% compares with consensus of 48.8% and guidance of 48%–49%, while JPMe EPS of $1.07 compares with consensus of $1.08 and guidance of $1.06–$1.08. JPMe gross margin is 62.8% versus consensus of 63.0%. 
  * 4Q26 Outlook: Revenue and earnings outlook to exceed JPMe and consensus expectations. JPMe 2026 revenue is $12.65 bn versus consensus of $12.69 bn. For 4Q, JPMe forecasts revenue of $3.61 bn versus consensus of $3.57 bn, operating margin of 47.9% versus 48.9%, and EPS of $1.14 versus $1.14.
  * Key Watch Points: Key watch points heading into the upcoming earnings print include commentary on the demand environment and risks as they relate to Tier 2/Neoclouds in particular, the magnitude and timing of the scale-up opportunity (including rack versus switch tray margins), as well as supply availability, especially related to the latest generation switching silicon. Furthermore, we would expect a focus on how Arista continues to navigate component cost inflation and the implications to gross margins. 



#

## Larger TAM and Customer Ramps Strengthen Case for Solid Initial 2027 Guide

### Historical guidance patterns point to a ~30% initial 2027 revenue growth
target

In recent years, Arista’s initial guidance for the following year has
typically landed near consensus, which currently calls for revenue growth of
+29% y/y and an operating margin of ~47% in 2027. If that pattern holds, we
expect Arista to begin the year with a revenue growth target of around +30%.

### Larger TAM of $340 bn+ by 2030 (30%+ CAGR) could support a more ambitious
initial 2027 guide

Historically, Arista has broken its TAM outlook into Data Center Ethernet
Switch and Campus Switch, along with a residual bucket containing software and
wireless, among other smaller markets (e.g., security, WAN). Since Arista
presented its $105 bn 2029 TAM in September 2025, which was based on 650
Group’s 1Q25 forecast, 650 Group has revised the 2029 DC Ethernet Switch TAM
by +170% (primarily on account of DC AI Switch) and the Campus Switch TAM by
+17%.

We expect the 2030 TAM presented alongside the 3Q26 earnings print to reflect
both revisions and, for the first time, include scale-up switching, which 650
Group sizes at $102 bn in 2030. We also see upside in the residual category as
Arista’s exposure to DCI expands. The DCI switching and routing market is
expected to expand from $4 bn in 2026 to $22 bn in 2030, implying a +56% CAGR.
Outside DCI, we conservatively assume the residual category grows at a +5%
CAGR over the remainder of the decade.

Taken together, these assumptions imply Arista’s TAM could expand at a 30%+
CAGR to $340 bn+ by 2030, including 40%+ growth in 2027. That larger
opportunity could give management room to set a more ambitious initial revenue
growth outlook ahead of the +30% range.

### Hyperscalers and AI Lab ramps to conservatively support at least 40%+
revenue growth in 2027

Combining our forecasts for hyperscaler revenue, the AI Lab customer’s TPU
ramp via Broadcom, and a conservative +5% y/y growth assumption for the
remaining business yields 2027 revenue growth of 40%+ y/y for Arista. That
compares with guidance for +40% y/y growth in 2026 and a +27% revenue CAGR
from 2022 to 2025. In our 2027 build, hyperscalers contribute roughly 25
percentage points of growth, the AI lab customer roughly 15 points, and the
remaining customers roughly 3 points. We see the latter assumption as a
readily identifiable source of upside.

With regard to the AI Lab customer, Broadcom has said it expects its AI Lab
customer to deploy 1 GW of TPUs in 2026, followed by another 5 GW in 2027, at
an estimated capex of $20-$30 bn per GW. We believe Arista could participate
in the scale-across network and/or spine layer, which together represent an
estimated ~10% of that spending. Assuming $125 bn of capex for the 5 GW
deployment in 2027 and a conservative share of the addressable opportunity, we
estimate Arista could generate $2 bn+ of revenue from the customer that year.

The rest of Arista’s business spans DCI/AI scale-across (+88% y/y market
growth in 2027), DC Ethernet Switch Ex-Hyperscaler and Neoclouds (+20% y/y),
and Campus Switching (+5% y/y). Our assumption of +5% y/y growth for this
business is therefore conservative as it matches the slowest growing of those
markets, even though much of Arista’s exposure is to faster growing data
center opportunities, likely representing low-hanging upside to our outlook.

# Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks

### Arista (Overweight; Price Target: $250.00)

### Investment Thesis

We rate Arista Overweight and expect further upside in revenue and earnings
estimates, led by 1) the continuation of the ramp in Arista’s AI revenues; 2)
a robust upgrade cycle for networking equipment with cloud customers; 3)
revenue upside from better-than-expected performance in Enterprise; 4) higher-
than-peer-group growth outlook in the long term.

### Valuation

We are maintaining our December 2027 price target of $250, based on valuing
our 2028E EPS estimate at a 45x P/E multiple. We believe our target P/E
multiple is appropriate as it represents a premium to the 2-year multiple
average of ~40x and a substantial premium to the long-term average of ~30x,
justified by visibility into accelerating growth driven by both the AI data
center build-out as well as Arista’s Enterprise opportunity.

### Risks to Rating and Price Target

#### Industry Downside Risks

Adoption of white box solutions remains a threat. While it is difficult to
drive superior performance using white box solutions (non-branded switches
available off the shelf) relative to switches from established technology
leaders like Arista or Cisco, the improving capabilities of the white box
solutions over time could drive customers to use them for parts of the network
with lower performance requirements. Faster-than-expected adoption of white
box solutions could imply downside to our Arista earnings forecasts and price
target.

#### Company-Specific Downside Risks

Faster-than-expected shift toward disaggregated software solutions from data
center customers could challenge Arista. Arista delivers industry-leading
switching technology through a combination of hardware and software, although
a significant portion of the value-add is driven by software. While Arista has
already started to offer disaggregated software products to its customers,
these do not yet account for a significant portion of revenues. A faster-than-
expected shift from customers toward proprietary software and generic hardware
could create competitive challenges for Arista.
